questions.question: Alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Sound a sharp horn blast when a child or any pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph could take up to ____ to come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs a long distance to stop. At 55 mph, it may take almost 400 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: You are driving along a street and hear a siren. You cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot see where the emergency vehicle is, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Stay stopped until you know it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: An approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles are often hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead in residential areas. Signal five seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: A motorist should know that a bicyclist operating on a roadway must:

options.text: Ride on the right side of the road.
Ride on the side of the road facing traffic.
Ride on either side of the road.
Ride on the side of the road with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must use a bike lane if one is available. If no bike lane exists, they must stay near the right edge of the road and ride in the same direction as traffic.

questions.question: You must yield the right-of-way to an approaching vehicle when you are:
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to traffic going straight or turning right. Drivers entering a traffic circle must yield to drivers already in the circle.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle on the right if it is:

options.text: Turning into a driveway on the right.

questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only in certain situations. You must not drive on or across the shoulder or edge line. You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn.

questions.question: You may park or stop on a freeway shoulder:

options.text: If you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: When passing a parked car on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
Assume the driver will wait until you pass to open the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for the driver to open the car door.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle that just parked, expect the driver to open the door as you approach. Drive with extra care near parked vehicles.

questions.question: If traffic blocks you from crossing railroad tracks completely, you may cross only when:

options.text: An approaching train is not moving fast enough to be dangerous.
Your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.
At least half of your vehicle can cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.
questions.explanation: Always make sure your entire vehicle will clear all tracks before crossing. If traffic blocks you, wait until there is enough room for your whole vehicle to cross.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: A car behind you starts to pass. You should:

options.text: Keep your speed steady so traffic flows smoothly.
Pull right and stop to let it pass.
Slow down a little and stay in your lane.
Honk your horn to signal it to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down a little and stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: When another vehicle passes you on the left, slow down slightly and stay to the right. Once it has safely passed, return to your normal speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign means there is a railroad crossing ahead. You will see it a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Your vehicle needs a longer distance to stop when:

options.text: The road is wet or icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet or icy.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.
